source_refs.note: Book p. 54-55: 2.10.4 Second Derivative Test (items 1-3; 'inclusive' misprint), Point to Note box, Example 21

blocks.text: 2.9.2 mein humne critical point ke dono taraf \(f'\) ka sign dekh kar faisla kiya tha ke wahan chotti hai ya wadi. Yeh kaam do test points maangta hai. Ab ek shortcut seekhte hain: Second Derivative Test. Is mein sirf ek number dekhna hota hai, \(f''(c)\), aur us ke sign se foran pata chal jata hai ke stationary point par maximum hai ya minimum. Exercise 2.4 ka poora Question 2 isi test par hai, is liye ise achhi tarah samajh lijiye.
Kitab ka bayan: maan lijiye \(f\) point \(x = c\) par do dafa differentiable hai, aur \(c\) function ke domain mein hai. Farz karein \(f'(c) = 0\). To:

items: Agar \(f''(c) < 0\) ho to \(f\) ka \(c\) par relative maximum hai.
Agar \(f''(c) > 0\) ho to \(f\) ka \(c\) par relative minimum hai.
Agar \(f''(c) = 0\) ho to test inconclusive hai (koi faisla nahin deta), aur critical point ki nature sirf second derivative test se maloom nahin ho sakti.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Item 3 mein kitab "the test is inclusive" chhaapti hai. Sahi lafz "inconclusive" hai, yani jab \(f''(c) = 0\) ho to test koi faisla nahin deta. ("Inclusive" ka matlab bilkul alag hai: shamil.)

blocks.title: Point to Note
blocks.text: If first derivative is not defined at a critical point, can we apply second derivative test at that critical point.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Point to Note ka jawab: nahin. Test ke liye \(f'(c) = 0\) aur \(f''(c)\) dono chahiye. Agar \(f'(c)\) hi exist nahin karta to \(f''(c)\) kaise hoga? Aise points par (jaise \(|x|\) ya \(x^{2/3}\) ka 0) wahi purana tareeqa: dono taraf \(f'\) ka sign (2.9.2).
Test kaam kyun karta hai? \(f''\) slope ke badalne ki raftaar hai. \(f''(c) < 0\) ka matlab slope ghat raha hai aur 0 se guzar raha hai: \(c\) se pehle positive (charhai), baad mein negative (utraai). Yani upar phir neeche: maximum. Curve ulte pyale (cup) ki tarah jhukta hai. \(f''(c) > 0\) ho to slope negative se positive: pehle utraai phir charhai, yani minimum. Curve seedhe pyale ki tarah hai jis mein paani thehar sakta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Jab \(f''(c) = 0\) ho to kuch bhi ho sakta hai. \(c = 0\) par: \(x^{4}\) ka minimum hai, \(-x^{4}\) ka maximum hai, aur \(x^{3}\) ka na maximum na minimum; lekin teeno mein \(f'(0) = f''(0) = 0\). Is liye aisi soorat mein dobara \(f'\) ke sign wala tareeqa lagaiye.

blocks.title: Example 21
blocks.problem: Examine the function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^{4} - \frac{4}{3}x^{3} - x^{2} + 4x + 1\) for relative extreme values.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^{4} - \frac{4}{3}x^{3} - x^{2} + 4x + 1\) ...(1).
Maloom karna: relative (local) maximum aur minimum values.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test. Pehle \(f'(x) = 0\) se stationary points, phir har point par \(f''\) ka sign batayega ke wahan maximum hai ya minimum.

Step 1: Pehla derivative
\[f'(x) = 2x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 2x + 4 \quad \text{...(2)}\]
Kyun: har term par power rule: \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot 4x^{3} = 2x^{3}\), \(\frac{4}{3} \cdot 3x^{2} = 4x^{2}\), \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{2}) = 2x\), \(\frac{d}{dx}(4x) = 4\), aur constant 1 ka derivative 0. Dekhiye fractions kaise khud ba khud cancel ho gaye.

Step 2: \(f'(x) = 0\) aur factorise
\[2x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 2x + 4 = 0\]
\[x^{3} - 2x^{2} - x + 2 = 0\]
\[x^{3} - x - 2x^{2} + 2 = 0\]
\[x(x^{2} - 1) - 2(x^{2} - 1) = 0\]
\[(x - 2)(x^{2} - 1) = 0\]
\[(x - 2)(x - 1)(x + 1) = 0\]
To critical points \(x = -1\), \(x = 1\), \(x = 2\) hain.
Kyun: pehle 2 se divide kiya. Phir terms ko joron mein tarteeb diya (grouping): \(x^{3} - x\) se \(x\) bahar, \(-2x^{2} + 2\) se \(-2\) bahar; dono mein \(x^{2} - 1\) common nikla. Aakhir mein \(x^{2} - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1)\).

Step 3: Doosra derivative
\[f''(x) = 6x^{2} - 8x - 2\]
\[= 2(3x^{2} - 4x - 1) \quad \text{...(3)}\]
Kyun: \(f'(x)\) ka ek dafa aur derivative liya.

Step 4: Har critical point ka test
\[f''(-1) = 2(3(-1)^{2} - 4(-1) - 1) = 12 > 0\]
\[f''(1) = 2(3(1)^{2} - 4(1) - 1) = -4 < 0\]
\[f''(2) = 2(3(2)^{2} - 4(2) - 1) = 6 > 0\]
Yani \(x = -1\) par relative minimum, \(x = 1\) par relative maximum, aur \(x = 2\) par relative minimum.
Kyun: \(f''(c) > 0\) yani pyala seedha (minimum), \(f''(c) < 0\) yani pyala ulta (maximum).
Dhyan dein: \(-4(-1) = +4\); is jagah sign ki ghalti bohat hoti hai.

Step 5: Equation (1) se values
\[f(-1) = \tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{4}{3} - 1 - 4 + 1 = -\tfrac{13}{6}\]
\[f(1) = \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{4}{3} - 1 + 4 + 1 = \tfrac{19}{6}\]
\[f(2) = 8 - \tfrac{32}{3} - 4 + 8 + 1 = \tfrac{7}{3}\]
Kyun: extreme values khud \(f\) ki values hain, is liye asal function (1) mein rakhte hain, \(f'\) ya \(f''\) mein nahin. Common denominator 6: \(\frac{3 + 8 - 24}{6} = -\frac{13}{6}\), \(\frac{3 - 8 + 24}{6} = \frac{19}{6}\), aur \(13 - \frac{32}{3} = \frac{7}{3}\).

Tasdeeq: \(f'\) ke signs bhi yahi kehte hain. \(f'(-2) = -24 < 0\), \(f'(0) = 4 > 0\), \(f'(1.5) = -1.25 < 0\), \(f'(3) = 16 > 0\): neeche, upar, neeche, upar. Yani minimum, maximum, minimum: bilkul wahi jo second derivative ne bataya.
blocks.answer: Relative minimum value \(f(-1) = -\frac{13}{6}\); relative maximum value \(f(1) = \frac{19}{6}\); relative minimum value \(f(2) = \frac{7}{3}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kab kaunsa test? Do raaste hain:
First derivative wala tareeqa (2.9.2): critical point ke dono taraf \(f'\) ka sign. Yeh har critical point par kaam karta hai, chahe wahan \(f'\) exist na kare, aur kabhi "faisla nahin" nahin kehta. Lekin is mein do test points ka hisaab karna parta hai.
Second Derivative Test (2.10.4): sirf \(f''(c)\) ka sign. Jab \(f''\) aasaani se nikal aaye (polynomials, \(e^{x}\) wale functions) to yeh tez hai. Lekin jab \(f''(c) = 0\) ho ya \(f'(c)\) exist na kare to yeh kaam nahin aata.
Exam mein jab sawal mein likha ho "Using the Second Derivative Test" (Exercise 2.4 ka Question 2) to yahi test lagana zaroori hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(f(x) = x^{4}\) par Second Derivative Test lagaiye. Kya faisla hota hai? (Jawab: \(f'(0) = 0\) aur \(f''(x) = 12x^{2}\), to \(f''(0) = 0\): test inconclusive. Lekin \(f'(x) = 4x^{3}\) left par negative, right par positive, is liye \(x = 0\) par minimum hai.)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Har critical point ke liye ek line: point, \(f''\) ki value us ke sign ke saath, natija, aur phir extreme value \(f(c)\). Fractions ko exact rakhiye (\(-\frac{13}{6}\), \(-2.17\) nahin), jab tak decimal na maanga jaye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Stationary point \(c\) (\(f'(c) = 0\)) par: \(f''(c) < 0\) relative maximum; \(f''(c) > 0\) relative minimum; \(f''(c) = 0\) koi faisla nahin.
2. Jahan \(f'(c)\) exist nahin karta wahan yeh test nahin lagta.
3. Extreme values asal \(f\) se aati hain.
4. Example 21: minima \(f(-1) = -\frac{13}{6}\), \(f(2) = \frac{7}{3}\); maximum \(f(1) = \frac{19}{6}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Rule ulta yaad karna: \(f'' < 0\) yani maximum, minimum nahin. (Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: minus = ulta pyala = chotti.)
2. \(f''(c) = 0\) par "koi extremum nahin" likh dena: test sirf khamosh hai, faisla \(f'\) se kijiye.
3. Extreme value ke liye \(c\) ko \(f'\) ya \(f''\) mein rakh dena, \(f\) ke bajaye.
